questionnaire.title: Family Ageing Questionnaire
intro: Tell us what's happening, and we'll help you work out what to do next.

This questionnaire prepares your free personalised Family Ageing Action Plan. Depending on your situation it takes around 10 to 15 minutes, and you will only be shown questions that are relevant to you.
You don't need to know every answer. “Not sure” is useful information too.
Please don't include account numbers, passwords, detailed medical records or other highly confidential information.
questionnaire.notice: Ageing Navigator provides independent ageing-related information and navigation. It does not provide medical diagnoses, legal or financial advice, or formal government needs assessments. If someone is in immediate danger or needs urgent medical attention, contact the appropriate emergency service.

actions.title: Deal with the urgent concern before anything else
actions.why: Some of what you told us may need attention straight away, ahead of the planning steps in this plan.
actions.nextStep: If anyone is in danger or needs urgent medical help, call 111. Otherwise contact the GP or the hospital team today.
questions: What should we do if this happens again?
check: Whether the urgent concern has been seen by a health professional
actions.whenText: q18 in yes, possibly or q18a answered

actions.title: Plan the discharge with the hospital team before the day
actions.why: Leaving hospital without the right support in place can lead to problems at home.
actions.nextStep: Ask to speak with the ward's discharge planner or social worker about what support will be in place at home.
prepare: A list of who can help in the first week
questions: What support will be in place on the first day home?
Who do we call if things are not working?
check: Whether equipment is arranged before discharge
actions.whenText: h1 in in_hospital, leaving_soon

actions.title: Check that support after hospital is working
actions.why: The weeks after a hospital stay are when extra help is most often needed.
actions.nextStep: Review with the GP or the hospital's community team whether the support arranged is enough.
questions: Is a follow-up appointment booked?
check: Whether any follow-up appointments have been missed
actions.whenText: h1 in discharged_home, discharged_other, repeat_visits

actions.title: Ask for a needs assessment
actions.why: A needs assessment is usually how access to publicly funded support at home, respite and residential care is decided. Ageing Navigator does not carry out this assessment.
actions.nextStep: Ask the GP for a referral to the local Needs Assessment and Service Coordination (NASC) service.
prepare: What help is needed each day and week
Recent falls, hospital visits or changes
questions: What support could the assessment lead to?
How long is the wait for an assessment?
check: Whether a referral has already been made
actions.whenText: q19 in none, thinking, dont_know_what, unsure and (q15 in probably_not, definitely_not, none or q13 in noticeably_more, significantly_more)

actions.title: Follow up the needs assessment referral
actions.why: Referrals can wait a long time without anyone noticing.
actions.nextStep: Call the NASC service to confirm the referral arrived and ask about the expected timing.
questions: When is the assessment likely to happen?
check: The date the referral was made
actions.whenText: q19 is requested

actions.title: Ask for a review of the current support
actions.why: Needs change, and support that was right a year ago may no longer be enough.
actions.nextStep: Contact the NASC service or the home support provider and ask for a review.
prepare: Examples of what is not working now
questions: Can the hours or type of support be reviewed?
actions.whenText: q19 in completed, receiving and q15 in probably_not, definitely_not

actions.title: Look at more help at home
actions.why: Help with personal care, meals, cleaning or shopping can make staying at home safer and take pressure off family.
actions.nextStep: List the tasks that need help, then compare funded and private options.
prepare: A list of tasks that need help, and how often
questions: What is available for free, and what would we pay?
Is there a minimum number of hours?
check: Costs and minimum hours of any private provider
actions.whenText: q15 in probably_not, definitely_not, none or (q14 has no_regular_support and q13 in noticeably_more, significantly_more)

actions.title: Talk to the GP about falls and ask about strength and balance classes
actions.why: Falls are a leading cause of injury for older people, and many can be prevented.
actions.nextStep: Book a GP appointment to discuss the falls, medication and balance.
prepare: When and where each fall happened
questions: Could any medication be affecting balance?
Is there a strength and balance class nearby?
actions.whenText: q17_falls in one, two_three, more or q17 has falling or q8 has falls or trigger has fall

actions.title: Look into a personal alarm
actions.why: Someone who lives alone may not be able to reach a phone after a fall.
actions.nextStep: Ask the GP or the NASC service whether a funded alarm may be available, and compare private options.
questions: Who would the alarm call, and what happens then?
actions.whenText: q6 is alone and (q17 has any falling, getting_help_in_an_emergency, being_alone or q17_falls in one, two_three, more)

actions.title: Ask for advice on making the home safer
actions.why: Rails, better lighting and the right equipment prevent many falls and make daily tasks easier.
actions.nextStep: Ask the GP about a referral to an occupational therapist for a home assessment.
prepare: The rooms and tasks that are hardest
questions: Which changes would make the biggest difference?
Is any equipment funded?
actions.whenText: q24 has any stairs, bathroom_safety, risk_of_falling, getting_around_the_home or q17 has any bathroom_safety, getting_in_or_out_of_bed_or_chairs

actions.title: Talk to the GP about the memory changes
actions.why: Memory changes have many possible causes, some treatable. Only a health professional can assess them.
actions.nextStep: Book a GP appointment and bring examples of what has changed.
prepare: Examples of what has changed, and since when
questions: Could anything else be causing this?
Is a memory assessment worth arranging?
actions.whenText: m1 in minor, concerned, affecting_daily_life, unsure

actions.title: Contact local dementia support services
actions.why: Dementia support services offer education, support groups and advice for the person and the family.
actions.nextStep: Contact the local dementia support organisation and ask what is available in the area.
questions: What support is there for family members?
actions.whenText: m1 in diagnosed, being_assessed or trigger has dementia_diagnosis

actions.title: Talk to the GP about driving safety
actions.why: Changes in health or memory can affect driving, and the GP can advise on fitness to drive.
actions.nextStep: Raise driving at the next GP appointment.
questions: Is a driving assessment needed?
actions.whenText: q17 has driving or q8 has driving or m2 has driving

actions.title: Get support for the family carer
actions.why: Carers who are exhausted cannot keep going, and support for them keeps care at home possible for longer.
actions.nextStep: Contact Carers NZ for information and ask the GP about support for the carer.
questions: What breaks or support are available for the carer?
actions.whenText: q16 in significant, some or q9 has an_unpaid_family_carer_is_struggling

actions.title: Find out about respite options
actions.why: Planned breaks help unpaid carers keep going.
actions.nextStep: Ask the NASC service whether respite may be available, and what the options are locally.
questions: How is respite arranged, and how far ahead?
check: Whether a needs assessment is needed first
actions.whenText: q16 is significant or q8 has respite

actions.title: Set up or check the Enduring Powers of Attorney
actions.why: An EPOA lets someone chosen in advance make decisions if the person can no longer do so. It can only be made while the person still has capacity.
actions.nextStep: Talk to a lawyer about making or checking both EPOAs (property, and personal care and welfare).
prepare: Who the person would want to act for them
questions: What does it cost, and how long does it take?
check: Whether existing documents can be found
actions.whenText: q21.epoa_property in no, unsure or q21.epoa_welfare in no, unsure

actions.title: Make or update a will
actions.why: A current will avoids delays and disagreements later.
actions.nextStep: Arrange a will with a lawyer or the Public Trust.
check: Where the current will is kept
actions.whenText: q21.will in no, unsure

actions.title: Talk about an advance care plan
actions.why: An advance care plan records what matters to the person for future health care.
actions.nextStep: Start the conversation, and ask the GP about recording an advance care plan.
actions.whenText: q21.advance_care_plan in no, unsure

actions.title: Find out about transport options
actions.why: Getting to appointments and activities affects health and independence.
actions.nextStep: Ask the local council about the Total Mobility scheme and community transport.
actions.whenText: q12 has transport or q8 has transport or q24 has lack_of_transport

actions.title: Look for social activities and visiting services
actions.why: Loneliness can affect health and wellbeing.
actions.nextStep: Contact Age Concern about visiting services and local activities.
actions.whenText: q8 has loneliness_or_social_isolation or q24 has social_isolation or q12 has companionship_or_social_contact

actions.title: Find out which funding pathways may be worth investigating
actions.why: Some support is publicly funded after a needs assessment; other costs are paid privately. Knowing the difference early avoids surprises.
actions.nextStep: Start with the needs assessment step in this plan, and note the funding questions to ask.
prepare: A broad idea of income and assets, if you are comfortable
questions: Which costs would be funded, and which would we pay?
actions.whenText: q20 in very_important, important or q8 has any government_funded_support, paying_for_care, understanding_what_support_they_may_be_entitled_to

actions.title: Make a shortlist of villages and ask for their disclosure statements
actions.why: Villages differ widely in fees, contracts, care on site and pet rules.
actions.nextStep: Choose three to five villages that fit what matters most and ask each for its disclosure statement.
prepare: What matters most in a village
questions: What is the weekly fee, and how can it change?
What is the deferred management fee?
What care is available on site if needs change?
check: Pet, care-suite and resale rules for each village
actions.whenText: q23 in village, serviced, planning_move or trigger has considering_village or q8 has retirement_villages

actions.title: Plan for independent legal advice before signing
actions.why: The law requires independent legal advice before signing an Occupation Right Agreement.
actions.nextStep: Choose a lawyer who knows retirement village contracts, before committing to a village.
questions: What happens to the capital when leaving the village?
actions.whenText: q23 in village, serviced, planning_move or trigger has considering_village or q8 has retirement_villages

actions.title: Ask how an assessment for residential care is arranged
actions.why: Whether residential care is needed, and at what level, is decided through a formal needs assessment. Ageing Navigator does not decide this.
actions.nextStep: Ask the GP or the NASC service how an assessment for residential care would be arranged.
questions: What levels of care might be considered?
check: Whether an assessment has already been done
actions.whenText: (q23 is residential_care or trigger has considering_residential or q8 has residential_care or q6 is residential_care) and (rc2 not answered or rc2 in none, unsure, other)

actions.title: Shortlist care homes that provide the assessed level of care
actions.why: Not every care home provides every level of care, and availability changes often.
actions.nextStep: List care homes in the preferred area that provide the assessed level, and call about availability.
questions: Is there a room available, and what does it cost?
Are there premium room charges?
actions.whenText: rc1 in assessment_identified, actively_looking, urgent and rc2 in rest_home, hospital, dementia, psychogeriatric

actions.title: Find out about the Residential Care Subsidy and Loan
actions.why: Work and Income decides who receives the Residential Care Subsidy or Loan, based on assets and income, after a needs assessment.
actions.nextStep: Read the Work and Income information and note the questions to ask.
prepare: A broad idea of assets and income
questions: Which assets are counted?
How long does an application take?
check: Current asset thresholds on the Work and Income website
actions.whenText: (q23 is residential_care or trigger has considering_residential or q8 has residential_care or q6 is residential_care) and (q20 in very_important, important or rc3 has any government_funding, costs)

actions.title: Agree who in the family will do what
actions.why: Plans stall when everyone assumes someone else is organising things.
actions.nextStep: Share this plan with the family and agree who takes each step.
actions.whenText: q26 in some_differences, significant_disagreement, not_discussed or q25 in nobody, unsure

actions.title: Talk with {{name}} about wishes for the future
actions.why: Knowing what {{name}} wants makes later decisions easier for everyone.
actions.nextStep: Find a calm time to talk about where {{name}} would like to live and what matters most.
actions.whenText: q23 in not_discussed, family_differs, unsure, open or trigger has planning_ahead

texts.home_heading: Something has changed. What should happen next?
texts.home_intro: A fall, a diagnosis, a hospital stay, or simply planning ahead. Answer a few questions about the situation and we will prepare a free, personalised Family Ageing Action Plan: the pathways worth exploring, what to do first, who can help, and what to ask.
texts.notice: Ageing Navigator provides independent ageing-related information and navigation. It does not provide medical diagnoses, legal or financial advice, or formal government needs assessments. If someone is in immediate danger or needs urgent medical attention, contact the appropriate emergency service.
texts.consent: Ageing Navigator will use your answers to prepare a personalised Family Ageing Action Plan. A navigator checks every plan before it is sent to you. Your answers are stored securely in Australia, seen only by the Ageing Navigator team, and deleted 12 months after your plan is sent, or sooner if you ask. We do not use AI, and we do not share your answers with anyone else without asking you first.
texts.consent_checkbox: I agree, and I have the older person's agreement or am acting in their interests.
texts.thank_you: Thank you. Your answers have reached Ageing Navigator. A navigator will check your personalised Action Plan and email it to you, usually within a few working days.
texts.urgent_guidance: If anyone is in immediate danger or needs urgent medical help, call 111 now. For health advice at any time, call Healthline on 0800 611 116. Please do not wait for your Action Plan.
texts.plan_intro: This plan brings together what you told us about {{name}}'s situation and the steps that may help next. Each step is a possible pathway to investigate, not a decision.
texts.plan_cover_note: This plan is private to your family. It is information and navigation, not medical, legal or financial advice.
texts.disclaimer: Ageing Navigator provides independent information and navigation. It does not provide medical diagnoses, legal or financial advice, or formal needs assessments, and it does not decide eligibility for any funding or service. Sources were checked on the dates shown.
texts.pathway_none: Your answers do not point to one pathway yet, which is common. The steps below help whatever you decide, and a navigator can help you think through the options.
texts.cta_default: Would you like Ageing Navigator to organise these next steps for you?
texts.email_release_subject: Your Family Ageing Action Plan is ready

Hello,

Your personalised Family Ageing Action Plan has been checked by a navigator and is ready.

Open your plan: {{link}}

This link is private to you. It works until {{expires}}. On the plan page you can download it as a PDF, and ask us for help with any of the steps.

Ageing Navigator
texts.request_intro: Tell us what you would like help with and a navigator will contact you to talk it through. There is no obligation, and we will tell you the cost before anything starts.
texts.request_done: Thank you. A navigator will contact you to talk it through.
texts.home_eyebrow: Free for families in the Bay of Plenty
texts.marketing_consent: Send me occasional news from Ageing Navigator. This is optional and you can stop at any time.
texts.cta_stay_home: Would you like Ageing Navigator to organise your Home Support Setup?
texts.cta_village: Would you like Ageing Navigator to help coordinate your Retirement Village Transition?

texts.feedback_intro: Ageing Navigator is being tested with a small number of families. Your answers help us make the plans better for the next family.
texts.questionnaire_intro:
Tell us what's happening, and we'll help you work out what to do next.

This questionnaire prepares your free personalised Family Ageing Action Plan. Depending on your situation it takes around 10 to 15 minutes, and you will only be shown questions that are relevant to you.

You don't need to know every answer. “Not sure” is useful information too.

Please don't include account numbers, passwords, detailed medical records or other highly confidential information.
texts.contact_intro: We only use these details to send the plan and to contact you about it.
